<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` (#50465), the memory profile run samples through the gathered `compute_logits` path. So the sharded path's `all_to_all_single` first runs in the kernel warm-up, after the KV cache has already taken the memory budget. On memory-tight GPUs, NCCL then cannot allocate its all-to-all buffers, and start-up fails. This PR makes `_dummy_sampler_run` call `sample()`, so the profile run takes the sharded path (all-to-all, local sampler, output gather) and those buffers exist before the KV cache is sized.

## Claims

- With batch-sharded sampling on, the profile run executes the same all-to-all as serving. NCCL's buffers for it are then counted in the memory profile, not allocated after the KV cache.
- No change when the flag is off.

## Validation

**Reproducer (measured):**
- Setup: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP8 + EP, 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, FP8 KV, MTP 3, `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`. The model support comes from #61018.
- Without this fix, start-up fails in `warmup_kernels` → `sample_tokens` → `all_to_all_logits` → `all_to_all_single`, with `RuntimeError: NCCL Error 1: unhandled cuda error`. On all 8 ranks the NCCL log shows `include/alloc.h:320 (ncclCuMemAlloc) NCCL WARN Cuda failure 2 'out of memory'`.
- Before the failure, every rank logged "Batch-sharded sampling enabled."

**With this fix (measured, same node type and command):** this end-to-end run used the first revision of this PR, which ran the same `shard_sampler_inputs` → `compute_logits_local` → `all_to_all_logits` sequence inline. The current revision reaches that sequence through `sample()` (review suggestion) and also runs the output all-gather. I have not re-run the end-to-end test on the current revision.
- Start-up passes warm-up on all 8 ranks. All ranks log "Batch-sharded sampling enabled.", there is no NCCL OOM, and the server answers requests.
- The memory profile now counts the all-to-all's NCCL buffers. Per GPU, at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`:

| | Flag off (control) | Flag on, with this fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Weights + non-torch memory | 17.75 GiB | 20.62 GiB (+2.87 GiB) |
| Peak activation | 1.98 GiB | 1.97 GiB |
| CUDA graphs | 0.71 GiB | 0.71 GiB |
| KV cache memory | 15.82 GiB | 12.95 GiB |
| KV cache size (tokens) | 2,128,699 | 1,742,619 (−18 %) |

- So on 40 GB GPUs, batch-sharded sampling costs about 2.9 GiB per GPU of NCCL point-to-point buffers. Without this fix, that memory is not reserved and start-up fails. With it, the cost is visible as a smaller KV cache. A possible mitigation for users is to limit NCCL point-to-point channels (for example `NCCL_MAX_P2P_NCHANNELS`), because this all-to-all moves only a few MB per step. I have not measured that yet.
- Serving (MLPerf agentic full set, 20 concurrent sessions, 3 × 60 min): the server ran all three repeats with no error. The goodput was lower than with the flag off (1.35–1.38 vs 1.83–1.89 req/s), because of the smaller KV cache on this capacity-bound workload; that is a property of batch-sharded sampling on 40 GB GPUs, not of this fix. Without this fix the same command does not start.

- `pre-commit run --files` on the two touched files (ruff check, ruff format, mypy, typos and the other hooks): pass.
- Unit tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py`:
  - `test_dummy_sampler_run_profiles_rank_without_local_reqs[0|3]` runs the real `sample()` for TP rank 0 and rank 3 of 4 with 3 dummy requests. On both ranks, both profile passes run the all-to-all and the output gather. Rank 0 owns a request and runs no fallback; rank 3 owns none and runs the local sampler once on a one-row batch. The test fails on `main` (the profile run does not take the sharded path); a fallback that always runs fails rank 0, and a fallback that never runs fails rank 3.
  - `test_num_local_reqs_follows_request_owners` checks `num_local_reqs` for round-robin owners and for a sharded draft logits owner table.
  - `pytest --noconftest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py`: 9 passed, 20 skipped (CUDA-only) on a CPU host. The OOM itself needs a multi-rank NCCL group and the memory pressure of a real model, so that validation is end to end (above).
- Duplicate check: no open PR or issue covers this (searched `batch-sharded profile all_to_all`, `sharded sampling OOM`).

### Re-test on main with the extensible KV cache (3 Nov 2026)

Same model and node type, nightly 76c6f3f2a9 (contains #56492, extensible KV cache, on by default) + #65225 + #61018, FP8 KV, `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, `--max-num-seqs 32`. Arm A without this PR, arm B with it. Each arm: start, then a probe (3 long-context needle checks, 6 fixed prompts, 16 concurrent requests).

| | A: without this PR | B: with this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Start-up and probe | pass, no NCCL OOM | pass |
| Profiled weights + non-torch memory (rank 0) | 17.89 GiB | 20.55 GiB (+2.66 GiB) |
| KV cache blocks committed after warm-up (rank 0) | 3,586 | 3,586 |
| GPU KV cache size (tokens) | 1,654,553 | 1,654,553 |

- With the extensible KV cache, the KV cache is sized after warm-up ("Memory after warmup ... 3586 KV cache blocks"), when the all-to-all's NCCL buffers already exist. So on current main with default settings the start-up failure does not occur, and this PR changes only the profiler's report, not the KV cache size.
- The failure path remains when the KV cache is sized from the profile, that is with `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` (or a configuration that turns the extensible KV cache off). Measured below (4 Nov 2026): the failure reproduces there on a recent nightly, and this PR fixes it.

### Re-test with `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` (4 Nov 2026)

Nightly 40941f2c4b (its `model_runner.py` and `batch_shard.py` are identical to main 0eb619dc52), same model and node type, FP8 KV, `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`. Arm A = nightly + #61018 (model support for batch-sharded sampling), arm B = A + this PR. One start per arm, then the same probe as above.

| | A: without this PR | B: with this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Available KV cache memory (rank 0, from the profile) | 13.35 GiB | 10.73 GiB (−2.62 GiB) |
| Start-up | **fails**: `torch.OutOfMemoryError` on all 8 ranks during CUDA graph capture (`capture_model`), 37 MiB free of 39.49 GiB | pass, GPU KV cache 1,479,175 tokens |
| Probe (3 needles, 6 fixed prompts, 16 concurrent) | not reached | pass |

- Without this PR, the profile does not see the all-to-all's NCCL buffers, so the KV cache takes about 2.6 GiB that the NCCL buffers need later, and the first allocation after that (here during graph capture) fails. The −2.62 GiB in arm B matches the +2.66 GiB profiler difference measured above.

## Details

- **Root cause:** `profile_run` → `_dummy_sampler_run` always called `self.model.compute_logits` (all-gather) and the sampler. `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` on the TP device group allocates its NCCL point-to-point buffers on first use. That first use was in `warmup_kernels`, which runs after `determine_available_memory` and the KV cache allocation.
- **Fix:** `_dummy_sampler_run` calls `self.sample(hidden_states, dummy_input_batch, None)` for the default pass and the warmup-param pass, so it stays in sync with `sample()`. All ranks reach the collectives, because `profile_run` runs on every worker.
- **Ranks with no dummy request:** `sample()` skips the local sampler on a rank that owns no request. When the dummy batch has fewer requests than TP ranks (`max_num_seqs < tp_size`), some ranks own no dummy request, but they can own a real request later. A rank for which the new `BatchSharder.num_local_reqs(idx_mapping_np)` returns 0 runs its local sampler once more on a one-row dummy batch (slot 0 has the warmup params). `num_local_reqs` uses the same owner lookup as `shard_sampler_inputs` (now shared in `BatchSharder._req_owners`), so the model runner does not depend on the assignment rule. Ranks can take different branches, because the fallback runs only the local sampler and has no collective. The one-row batch is built after both `sample()` passes, because `InputBatch.make_dummy` rewrites the shared `input_buffers`.
- **Size:** +12 / −4 lines in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` (profile path only) and +18 / −9 lines in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/batch_shard.py`.
- **Trade-off:** the KV cache is smaller by the size of the NCCL all-to-all buffers. That memory was needed anyway; without the fix, start-up fails instead.

---

Thanks for identifying this issue! Left a suggestion for how to make it more robust

To avoid duplicating this code from `sample`, what are your thoughts on just calling `sample()` inside `_dummy_sampler_run` instead, like this:

```
@torch.inference_mode()
def _dummy_sampler_run(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    num_reqs = hidden_states.shape[0]
    dummy_input_batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(
        num_reqs, num_reqs, self.input_buffers
    )
    # Default pass: ...
    self.sample(hidden_states, dummy_input_batch, None)
    if current_platform.is_cpu():
        return
    # Warmup-param pass: ...
    warmup_params = SamplingParams.for_sampler_warmup()
    for req_idx in range(num_reqs):
        self.sampler.add_request(req_idx, warmup_params)
    self.sampler.apply_staged_writes()
    self.sample(hidden_states, dummy_input_batch, None)
```

This allows the dummy run to stay in sync with future changes to `sample()`

- The memory profile now counts the all-to-all's NCCL buffers. Per GPU, at `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`:

| | Flag off (control) | Flag on, with this fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Weights + non-torch memory | 17.75 GiB | 20.62 GiB (+2.87 GiB) |
| Peak activation | 1.98 GiB | 1.97 GiB |
| CUDA graphs | 0.71 GiB | 0.71 GiB |
| KV cache memory | 15.82 GiB | 12.95 GiB |
| KV cache size (tokens) | 2,128,699 | 1,742,619 (−18 %) |

- So on 40 GB GPUs, batch-sharded sampling costs about 2.9 GiB per GPU of NCCL point-to-point buffers. Without this fix, that memory is not reserved and start-up fails. With it, the cost is visible as a smaller KV cache. A possible mitigation for users is to limit NCCL point-to-point channels (for example `NCCL_MAX_P2P_NCHANNELS`), because this all-to-all moves only a few MB per step. I have not measured that yet.
- Serving (MLPerf agentic full set, 20 concurrent sessions, 3 × 60 min): the server ran all three repeats with no error. The goodput was lower than with the flag off (1.35–1.38 vs 1.83–1.89 req/s), because of the smaller KV cache on this capacity-bound workload; that is a property of batch-sharded sampling on 40 GB GPUs, not of this fix. Without this fix the same command does not start.

- `pre-commit run --files` on the two touched files (ruff check, ruff format, mypy, typos and the other hooks): pass.
- Unit tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py`:
  - `test_dummy_sampler_run_profiles_rank_without_local_reqs[0|3]` runs the real `sample()` for TP rank 0 and rank 3 of 4 with 3 dummy requests. On both ranks, both profile passes run the all-to-all and the output gather. Rank 0 owns a request and runs no fallback; rank 3 owns none and runs the local sampler once on a one-row batch. The test fails on `main` (the profile run does not take the sharded path); a fallback that always runs fails rank 0, and a fallback that never runs fails rank 3.
  - `test_num_local_reqs_follows_request_owners` checks `num_local_reqs` for round-robin owners and for a sharded draft logits owner table.
  - `pytest --noconftest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py`: 9 passed, 20 skipped (CUDA-only) on a CPU host. The OOM itself needs a multi-rank NCCL group and the memory pressure of a real model, so that validation is end to end (above).
- Duplicate check: no open PR or issue covers this (searched `batch-sharded profile all_to_all`, `sharded sampling OOM`).

### Re-test on main with the extensible KV cache (3 Nov 2026)

Same model and node type, nightly 76c6f3f2a9 (contains #56492, extensible KV cache, on by default) + #65225 + #61018, FP8 KV, `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling`, `--max-num-seqs 32`. Arm A without this PR, arm B with it. Each arm: start, then a probe (3 long-context needle checks, 6 fixed prompts, 16 concurrent requests).

| | A: without this PR | B: with this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Start-up and probe | pass, no NCCL OOM | pass |
| Profiled weights + non-torch memory (rank 0) | 17.89 GiB | 20.55 GiB (+2.66 GiB) |
| KV cache blocks committed after warm-up (rank 0) | 3,586 | 3,586 |
| GPU KV cache size (tokens) | 1,654,553 | 1,654,553 |

- With the extensible KV cache, the KV cache is sized after warm-up ("Memory after warmup ... 3586 KV cache blocks"), when the all-to-all's NCCL buffers already exist. So on current main with default settings the start-up failure does not occur, and this PR changes only the profiler's report, not the KV cache size.
- The failure path remains when the KV cache is sized from the profile, that is with `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` (or a configuration that turns the extensible KV cache off). Measured below (4 Nov 2026): the failure reproduces there on a recent nightly, and this PR fixes it.

### Re-test with `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` (4 Nov 2026)

Nightly 40941f2c4b (its `model_runner.py` and `batch_shard.py` are identical to main 0eb619dc52), same model and node type, FP8 KV, `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache`. Arm A = nightly + #61018 (model support for batch-sharded sampling), arm B = A + this PR. One start per arm, then the same probe as above.

| | A: without this PR | B: with this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Available KV cache memory (rank 0, from the profile) | 13.35 GiB | 10.73 GiB (−2.62 GiB) |
| Start-up | **fails**: `torch.OutOfMemoryError` on all 8 ranks during CUDA graph capture (`capture_model`), 37 MiB free of 39.49 GiB | pass, GPU KV cache 1,479,175 tokens |
| Probe (3 needles, 6 fixed prompts, 16 concurrent) | not reached | pass |

- Without this PR, the profile does not see the all-to-all's NCCL buffers, so the KV cache takes about 2.6 GiB that the NCCL buffers need later, and the first allocation after that (here during graph capture) fails. The −2.62 GiB in arm B matches the +2.66 GiB profiler difference measured above.

## Details

- **Root cause:** `profile_run` → `_dummy_sampler_run` always called `self.model.compute_logits` (all-gather) and the sampler. `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` on the TP device group allocates its NCCL point-to-point buffers on first use. That first use was in `warmup_kernels`, which runs after `determine_available_memory` and the KV cache allocation.
- **Fix:** `_dummy_sampler_run` calls `self.sample(hidden_states, dummy_input_batch, None)` for the default pass and the warmup-param pass, so it stays in sync with `sample()`. All ranks reach the collectives, because `profile_run` runs on every worker.
- **Ranks with no dummy request:** `sample()` skips the local sampler on a rank that owns no request. When the dummy batch has fewer requests than TP ranks (`max_num_seqs < tp_size`), some ranks own no dummy request, but they can own a real request later. A rank for which the new `BatchSharder.num_local_reqs(idx_mapping_np)` returns 0 runs its local sampler once more on a one-row dummy batch (slot 0 has the warmup params). `num_local_reqs` uses the same owner lookup as `shard_sampler_inputs` (now shared in `BatchSharder._req_owners`), so the model runner does not depend on the assignment rule. Ranks can take different branches, because the fallback runs only the local sampler and has no collective. The one-row batch is built after both `sample()` passes, because `InputBatch.make_dummy` rewrites the shared `input_buffers`.
- **Size:** +12 / −4 lines in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` (profile path only) and +18 / −9 lines in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/batch_shard.py`.
- **Trade-off:** the KV cache is smaller by the size of the NCCL all-to-all buffers. That memory was needed anyway; without the fix, start-up fails instead.

To avoid duplicating this code from `sample`, what are your thoughts on just calling `sample()` inside `_dummy_sampler_run` instead, like this:

```
@torch.inference_mode()
def _dummy_sampler_run(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    num_reqs = hidden_states.shape[0]
    dummy_input_batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(
        num_reqs, num_reqs, self.input_buffers
    )
    # Default pass: ...
    self.sample(hidden_states, dummy_input_batch, None)
    if current_platform.is_cpu():
        return
    # Warmup-param pass: ...
    warmup_params = SamplingParams.for_sampler_warmup()
    for req_idx in range(num_reqs):
        self.sampler.add_request(req_idx, warmup_params)
    self.sampler.apply_staged_writes()
    self.sample(hidden_states, dummy_input_batch, None)
```

This allows the dummy run to stay in sync with future changes to `sample()`

Thanks @njhill, agreed that the extensible KV cache removes the estimate in most cases. I checked how it meets this fix on current main (76c6f3f2a9): with the extensible cache, `_compile_or_warm_up_model` resets the peak stats and then runs `_dummy_run` + `_dummy_sampler_run`, and `measure_kv_cache_blocks` keeps that measured peak free. So the batch-sharded all-to-all buffers are counted only if `_dummy_sampler_run` allocates them, which is what this PR makes it do (including the rank with no local dummy request). Without it, they first appear at the first real step, after the cache size is committed, and only the margin covers them. So I think the change stays useful in both paths: the fallback estimate path, and the measured warmup peak of the extensible path. I have not measured the extensible path end to end yet.
